name: Urinary Tract Arteriovenous Malformation

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of abnormal arteriovenous shunting within the urinary tract on angiography or contrast-enhanced imaging
Presence of recurrent or persistent gross hematuria unexplained by other causes
Histological confirmation of abnormal direct arterial to venous connections in urinary tract tissue biopsy
Exclusion of other causes of hematuria and vascular malformations such as tumors or trauma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiologic evidence of AVM in the urinary tract combined with recurrent gross hematuria and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological confirmation is supportive but not mandatory if imaging and clinical features are definitive.

searchTerms: frequent episodes of urine with blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulsatile bruit over the affected urinary tract region
pathognomonic.notes: Detected on auscultation or Doppler ultrasound

common.symptomName: Flank pain due to vascular engorgement or hemorrhage
common.notes: Often intermittent and associated with hematuria
searchTerms: side pain from blood vessel swelling or bleeding
flank discomfort due to vascular issues
pain caused by blood vessel problems in side

common.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
common.notes: May require transfusion in severe cases
searchTerms: low red blood cells from ongoing blood loss

common.notes: Rarely detected unless large AVM present

searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney blood flow problems
hypertension due to reduced kidney circulation
raised blood pressure from kidney ischemia

occasional.notes: Due to blood stasis or mucosal irritation

searchTerms: unstable blood pressure from sudden bleeding
shock caused by heavy blood loss

occasional.notes: Due to mass effect or clot formation

searchTerms: heart failure with high blood flow

laboratory: Microscopic or gross hematuria on urinalysis
Anemia with low hemoglobin and hematocrit
Elevated serum creatinine in advanced cases
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing early venous filling and vascular nidus
Digital subtraction angiography demonstrating direct arterial to venous connections
Doppler ultrasound revealing turbulent flow and pulsatile venous signals
genetic: No well-established genetic mutations identified; usually sporadic
other: Histopathology showing abnormal direct arteriovenous channels without intervening capillaries

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of solid renal mass on imaging
Systemic symptoms such as weight loss and fever
Benign vascular tumor with well-circumscribed lesion
Lack of direct arteriovenous shunting on angiography

redFlags: Sudden onset of massive hematuria with hemodynamic instability
references: Lee BB, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of arteriovenous malformations of the urinary tract. J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord. 2022;10(3):567-575.
